checks.evidence: Proofs in the rust provider (links/service_test/aliases_test.rs, fact_extraction/service_test.rs use_scopes, project/contract_test.rs) on synthetic facts and parsed sources.

(A) through_uses (links/service.rs) filters the in-scope bindings and takes min_by_key on the scope size, with a file-top use (no scope) at u32::MAX, so the innermost use shadows the outer ones, as in Rust. The new case an_alias_in_a_block_shadows_one_of_the_same_name_at_the_file_top expects the other.rs target; reverting to `find` would give shared.rs and fail it. (B) scope_of (fact_extraction/service.rs) records the span of the innermost StmtList or ItemList for every use not at the file top, and through_uses requires that span to hold the path. Same-named inline modules in sibling functions therefore stay apart: case an_alias_in_an_inline_module_leaves_a_path_in_another_module_of_the_same_name_to_the_crate, which would fail on the name chain alone. Every span in the six aliases_test cases and in use_scopes (a:7..45 b:16..26 c:33..43) was recomputed from its source text and matches. (C) linked() decodes each note once. Empty bytes are no note; any other bytes that fail to decode propagate NotesError, which converts to ProjectError::Context (outbound/notes/errors.rs). Case bytes_that_hold_no_note_refuse_the_links_and_lose_no_file_without_a_word expects the refusal. cargo check -p idiomatic-sh-ryo-rust --all-targets on an archive copy: 0 errors; the one warning (contract.rs:311, unnecessary qualification) predates this branch. The tests remain unrun here (hook), and are listed for the integrator.
No boundary change. From<NotesError> for ryo::languages::ProjectError is a conversion into the SDK's public error type, implemented in the provider (orphan rule allows it: NotesError is local).
One alias resolver (through_uses) and one note decode per file. The double decode (declared, then facts) is gone.
Direction unchanged: domain fact_extraction → fact_notes → links; the inbound contract maps the outbound adapter's error at the edge.
Fixtures are test-only; trees_agree compares the hand tree with the real parser.

tm_claim: Verified. tm's import_rows::service::in_scope (f1c9e1c968, service.rs:144-169) never compares module names. It takes the innermost scope holding the `use` by span size from syntax-tree stmt-list/item-list rows, requires that span to hold the edge, and shuts on any item-list span strictly inside it that holds the edge. Same-named inline modules have different spans, so variant B does not apply to tm.
error_names_no_file: Advisory. The refusal reads 'the bytes are not exactly one note' without the file, so a user with one stale or corrupt note cannot tell which file to fix. It is a loud refusal, not a silent loss, so it is not a leak. The no-string-literals rule does not force the omission: a constant prefix plus the request file's path (request.files at the same index) in the ToolMessage, or a NotesError variant carrying the path, would name it without a literal.
files_at_400: links/service.rs and project/contract.rs are each exactly 400 lines. file-length 0.3.0 refuses only above max-lines = 400, so both pass, but neither has headroom: the next edit to either must split it by role. Not a leak.
